question_text: Find the vertex, focus, equation of the directrix and axis of the parabola x² = −4y.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find a and the direction
steps.margin_note: First mark, for a = 1 and noticing the parabola opens downward.
lines: This is a downward parabola (the y-axis is
steps.why: Comparing the given equation to the standard downward form x² = −4ay is what fixes a, the one number every other answer in this question depends on.
common_mistakes: Comparing to y² = 4ax instead, which is the sideways form, not the up-down form this equation actually is.
Missing the minus sign and treating this as an upward parabola.
steps.memory_tip: x² with y alone means a vertical parabola; the minus sign in x² = −4ay means it opens downward.

steps.label: Sketch the downward parabola
steps.margin_note: Worth no mark by itself; it is a quick check that the direction found above is right.
steps.why: A quick sketch of the curve opening downward from the origin, with the focus marked below it, is the fastest way to check the four answers below make sense together — the focus must sit inside the curve, on the side it opens toward.
common_mistakes: Drawing the curve opening upward instead of downward.
Placing S above the vertex instead of below it.
steps.memory_tip: The curve opens toward the focus — draw the curve first, then put S on the inside of it.

steps.label: State the focus, directrix and axis
steps.margin_note: Second mark, for all four answers together, matching the downward direction found in step 1.
lines: (iii) Equation of the directrix: y = a ⇒ y − 1 = 0

lines.text: (iv) Axis of the parabola: x = 0 (the y-axis)

steps.why: For the standard downward form x² = −4ay the vertex is again the origin, but now the focus and directrix sit above and below on the y-axis rather than left-right on the x-axis, since the whole picture is rotated 90° from the familiar y² = 4ax case.
common_mistakes: Writing the focus as (0, a) instead of (0, −a) — the sign matters because the parabola opens downward.
Giving the axis as y = 0 instead of x = 0.
steps.memory_tip: For x² = −4ay: vertex at the origin, focus at (0,−a) below it, directrix at y = a above it, axis is the y-axis itself (x = 0).

insider_note: This question is the mirror image of a sideways parabola such as y² = 16x, with x and y exchanged and the direction flipped — the same four facts, rotated 90° and reflected.
